name: Italy — Italian parties
intro: compare it with Italian political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of Italy: those represented in the Chamber of Deputies and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the Chamber of Deputies after the September 2022 general election, arranged left to right. Approximate. 400 members.

AVS.name: Alleanza Verdi e Sinistra
AVS.priorities: Climate action, Workers' rights and wages, Public services, Diplomacy with Russia, no arms deliveries
AVS.description: Alliance of Europa Verde and Sinistra Italiana. It combines environmentalism with left-wing economics, calls for a minimum wage and opposes sending arms to Ukraine.

M5S.name: Movimento 5 Stelle
M5S.priorities: Minimum income and anti-poverty, Justice reform, Diplomacy with Russia, no arms deliveries, Climate action, Direct democracy
M5S.description: Founded as an anti-establishment movement by Beppe Grillo, now led by former prime minister Giuseppe Conte and closer to the left. It created the citizens' income, is tough on corruption and opposes arms for Ukraine.

PD.name: Partito Democratico
PD.priorities: Public healthcare, Workers' rights and wages, Public services, Deeper European integration, Climate action
PD.description: The main party of the Italian centre-left and the largest opposition force. Under Elly Schlein it has moved left, campaigning for public healthcare, a minimum wage and civil rights.

Volt.name: Volt Italia
Volt.priorities: Deeper European integration, Climate action, Digital innovation, Democratic reform
Volt.description: National chapter of Volt Europa, the first pan-European party. All chapters share one programme: a federal and more democratic EU, evidence-based policy, a market economy with a strong welfare state, and the digital and climate transitions. Volt has the same positions in every country in this test.

IV.name: Italia Viva
IV.priorities: Competitiveness and growth, Deeper European integration, Education, Justice reform
IV.description: Centrist party founded by former prime minister Matteo Renzi after leaving the PD. Liberal and pro-European, it has drawn closer to the centre-left opposition.

Azione.name: Azione
Azione.priorities: Nuclear energy, Competitiveness and growth, Education, Defence and support for Ukraine
Azione.description: Liberal, reformist party led by Carlo Calenda. It backs a return to nuclear power, industrial policy, fiscal responsibility and firm support for Ukraine.

FI.name: Forza Italia
FI.priorities: Lower taxes, Justice reform, Competitiveness and growth, Deeper European integration
FI.description: The party founded by Silvio Berlusconi, now the moderate, pro-European wing of Giorgia Meloni's governing coalition. It wants lower taxes, a flat tax and justice reform.

FdI.name: Fratelli d'Italia
FdI.ideologies: National conservatism, Conservatism, Soft Euroscepticism, Atlanticism
FdI.priorities: Reducing immigration, Traditional family values, Directly elected head of government, Security and law and order, Defence and support for Ukraine
FdI.description: Giorgia Meloni's party, first in 2022 and leading the government. National-conservative with post-fascist roots, it is hard-line on migration and traditional on family issues but pro-NATO and supportive of Ukraine.

Lega.name: Lega
Lega.priorities: Reducing immigration, Lower taxes, Regional autonomy, Security and law and order, Nuclear energy
Lega.description: Once a northern autonomist party, Matteo Salvini turned it into a national right-wing populist force. Part of the government, it pushes a flat tax, regional autonomy and closed ports, and is sceptical of the EU and of sanctions on Russia.
